collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and an adult)

collection.description: An elder laughs at a villager's ancient pendant, having watched it carved as a child: ask for the story, or keep the legend going.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) has always been told that the carved bone pendant (friend.he/she) wears is ancient, handed down for nobody knows how many generations, made by the first carver on Isola. Today, at the fire, (subject) looks at it for a long while and then starts laughing. "That? I watched an old carver make that. On a rainy afternoon. When I was about ten."

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) tells it: a bored carver, a rainy week, a bet about who could carve the most "ancient-looking" thing. The pendant won. Somewhere along the way the story got bigger. (friend) holds the pendant and laughs until (friend.he/she) cries. "I've been telling people it's the oldest thing in the village." "Well," says (subject), "it's old NOW."

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) begs (subject) not to tell anyone. (subject) thinks about it, then winks. The pendant stays "ancient." (friend) wears it with just as much pride, plus a private joke. Years later, (friend.he/she) catches (friend.him/her)self telling a child that it was made by the first carver on Isola, and stops, and smiles, and doesn't correct it.
